# Sum vs treatment coding
If afex is not told "check_contrasts = FALSE" then it will check and change contrasts to be sum contrasts
For looking at the model estimates for correlations, when using sum contrasts, it's comparing against a grand mean.
Time pre = +1 and post = -1, so the interaction effect is half of the difference in slope between the two, and 
if it's negative, then it means that the post has a larger slow than the pre. 

For ANOVA-style output, the sum contrasts are important.
Have to decide when doing the correlation-like output if treatment makes more sense. Depends on what I want to show.

This should be at least approx step of how to add the model prediction lines to the raw data

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

pred <- ggpredict(model, terms = c("SciEfficacy_score", "Time"))

p +
  geom_line(data = pred,
            aes(x = x, y = predicted, color = group),
            size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred,
              aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = group),
              alpha = 0.2,
              color = NA)

```
